project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence: Root cause / sink: NamedScriptResourceCollector.java:113 (getWeightedResources) -- `current = getResource(resolver, location.getPath() + '/' + this.scriptName.substring(0, pos), useResourceCaching);` -- which funnels into AbstractResourceCollector.java:161-171 (getResource) -> AbstractResourceCollector.java:286-317 (getResourceOrNull, sink `resolver.getResource(path)` at line 317). Trust boundary: `path`/`scriptName` originates from a caller of the PUBLIC ServletResolver API methods SlingServletResolver#resolveServlet(Resource,String) and #resolveServlet(ResourceResolver,String) (SlingServletResolver.java:483-488, request==null branch -> NamedScriptResourceCollector.create(scriptNameOrResourceType, resource, executionPaths, useResourceCaching)), i.e. an untrusted "named script" identifier crossing into filesystem/repository path construction with no normalization or allow-listing on that specific branch -- unlike the immediately preceding sibling branch in the same method (NamedScriptResourceCollector.java:95-103) which DOES call ResourceUtil.normalize()+SlingServletResolver.isPathAllowed() before resolving. Verified empirically: MockResourceResolverFactory-backed ResourceResolver.getResource() normalizes ".." itself (confirmed via javap decompilation of MockResourceResolver.getResourceInternal(), which calls ResourceUtil.normalize(path) first), so `location.getPath()+"/"+"../../../secret/admin"` correctly resolves to "/secret/admin" outside the intended subtree. Every distinct sink/path a complete fix must cover: (1) NamedScriptResourceCollector.java:113 -- the un-normalized, un-allowlisted intermediate resource fetch built from `scriptName` (the PoV's primary target). (2) ResourceCollector.java:275 -- `current = resolver.getResource(current, selector);` inside getWeightedResources(), which walks the resource tree one raw request-selector segment at a time via ScriptResourceResolver.getResource(Resource,String) with no normalization of the intermediate `current` resource either (final add is filtered by isPathAllowed(child.getPath(),...) at ResourceCollector.java:234, but the intermediate traversal itself is unchecked, same asymmetry as (1)). (3) SlingServletResolver.java:457-460 -- the absolute-scriptPath branch IS guarded (ResourceUtil.normalize + isPathAllowed) but that guard is a no-op whenever `executionPaths` is unconfigured/null (SlingServletResolver.isPathAllowed returns true unconditionally when executionPaths is null/empty, SlingServletResolver.java:746-750) -- i.e. the allow-list mechanism itself provides no real containment under the common default (unconfigured) deployment, so any fix must not rely solely on `executionPaths` being configured. (4) AbstractResourceCollector.getResourceOrNull/getResource (lines 161-171, 286-318) are the shared generic sink reached by all of the above plus by ScriptResourceResolver.getResource(String)/getResource(Resource,String) (ScriptResourceResolver.java:56-104) and the ScriptResource re-fetch path (ScriptResource.java:64-67, `perThreadResolver.getResource(this.path)`) traced through MergingServletResourceProvider/ServletResourceProvider/ServletResource -- these re-resolve a previously-obtained path on a different, live ResourceResolver instance without re-validation; a hardening fix should ensure this generic sink itself enforces containment/allow-listing centrally rather than relying on each caller to remember to gate it.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: NamedScriptResourceCollector.create("../../../secret/admin/leak", contentResource, null /*executionPaths*/, false).getServlets(resolver, Collections.emptyList()) returns a resource whose path is "/secret/admin/leak.esp" -- a resource that lives completely outside the resource's own resourceType-derived script location "/apps/myapp/comp". The PoV asserts this (assertTrue(foundPaths.contains("/secret/admin/leak.esp"))), so it exits 0 on unpatched code and exits non-zero once a fix prevents the escape (verified: applying a containment check -- normalizing the intermediate path and requiring it stay within the location subtree, mirroring the sibling branch's ResourceUtil.normalize()+isPathAllowed() pattern -- makes the same assertion fail).
parsed_output.notes: Targeted trace: the alert's traces all converge on the generic AbstractResourceCollector.getResourceOrNull sink (lines 286/317, `resolver.getResource(path)`) reached transitively through ScriptResourceResolver -> MergingServletResourceProvider -> ServletResourceProvider/ServletResource -> SlingServletResolver -> ScriptResource. I chose NamedScriptResourceCollector.java:113 as the primary PoV target (rather than trying to drive the exact SlingServletResolver:460/ScriptResource:67 re-fetch hop shown in the traces) because: (1) it is a self-contained, directly demonstrable root cause -- a clear code asymmetry between two adjacent branches of the same method, one validated (lines 95-103) and one not (lines 106-115); (2) it is reachable through the same public API entry points the traces terminate at (SlingServletResolver#resolveServlet(Resource,String)/#resolveServlet(ResourceResolver,String) -> NamedScriptResourceCollector.create at SlingServletResolver.java:487); (3) it is exercisable deterministically in a fast unit test using the project's own existing test infrastructure (MockResourceResolverFactory/MockResourceResolverFactoryOptions, same pattern as HelperTestBase used by ResourceCollectorTest and AbstractResourceCollectorTest in this module) without needing to stand up the full OSGi-activated SlingServletResolver component; (4) I empirically verified (by temporarily patching NamedScriptResourceCollector with a containment+normalize check and re-running the PoV, then reverting) that this exact code path is both the cause of the vulnerable result and that a correct fix at this location makes the PoV fail as required. The PoV intentionally sets executionPaths=null to model the realistic, common "unconfigured" deployment default (confirmed via SlingServletResolver.isPathAllowed(), which is a no-op when executionPaths is null/empty) -- this is what makes the vulnerability genuinely exploitable end-to-end rather than merely an internal-fetch-then-filtered-out situation.
parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant a correct fix must enforce, uniformly at every path listed above (not just the one branch already guarded): any resource path built by concatenating a caller/request-derived path fragment (script name, request selector, scriptPath) onto a trusted base/location path must (a) be normalized (ResourceUtil.normalize) and rejected if normalization fails (returns null, i.e. attempted to walk above root), AND (b) be verified to remain within the intended restricted directory -- either the specific `location`/resourceType script-folder subtree the lookup is scoped to, and/or a properly-configured `executionPaths` allow-list -- BEFORE the path is used to resolve a resource, not only when adding the final candidate to results. Do not rely on `SlingServletResolver.isPathAllowed(path, executionPaths)` alone as the sole gate, since it is a permissive no-op when `executionPaths` is null/empty (the common unconfigured default) -- containment relative to the lookup's own location must hold independent of that optional allow-list. Known bypass variants / sibling call sites the fix must also block: (1) NamedScriptResourceCollector scriptName containing "../" segments anywhere before the final "/" (the PoV's exact vector), including encoded/mixed variants like "..%2f..%2f", "..\\..\\", doubled slashes "..//../", or a scriptName that is itself an absolute path smuggled in after a partial relative prefix; (2) ResourceCollector's selector-driven descent (`resolver.getResource(current, selector)`), where a request selector segment equal to ".." (e.g. URL `/content/page/..%2f..%2fsecret.selectorX.html` or literal ".." as a selector) walks `current` outside the resource's own children even though the final emitted candidate is still isPathAllowed-filtered -- the intermediate walk itself should be constrained; (3) the SlingServletResolver.java:457-460 absolute-scriptPath branch when `executionPaths` is left at its default/unset value -- add a non-bypassable containment check there too, don't assume administrators will configure `servletresolver.paths`; (4) the ScriptResource re-fetch at ScriptResource.java:67 (`perThreadResolver.getResource(this.path)`) and the ScriptResourceResolver/MergingServletResourceProvider/ServletResourceProvider chain -- ensure re-resolution of an already-validated path on a different resolver instance can't be abused to reach a different real resource than what was originally validated (e.g. via provider/mount reconfiguration between validation and use).
parsed_output.summary: Created a JUnit PoV proving CWE-22 path traversal in org.apache.sling.servlets.resolver.internal.helper.NamedScriptResourceCollector#getWeightedResources(Set, Resource). When a caller-supplied "script name" contains '../' segments, the collector concatenates it onto the trusted location path and resolves it via AbstractResourceCollector's getResource()/getResourceOrNull() -> ResourceResolver#getResource(String) sink WITHOUT the ResourceUtil.normalize()+SlingServletResolver.isPathAllowed() gate that its sibling ("extension") branch in the very same method already applies. This lets a script-name argument escape the resource's own resourceType script folder (e.g. "/apps/myapp/comp") and resolve/return an arbitrary out-of-tree resource elsewhere in the repository (e.g. "/secret/admin/leak.esp"), which SlingServletResolver then treats as a candidate script/servlet.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: NamedScriptResourceCollector.getWeightedResources() (path-segment branch, formerly lines ~106-115) and ResourceCollector.getWeightedResources() (selector-driven descent, formerly line ~275) both resolved an intermediate Resource by concatenating/descending with a caller-controlled fragment onto a trusted `location` path, without normalizing or checking that the result stayed within that location's subtree. Fix:
1. Added `AbstractResourceCollector.isContained(String basePath, String path)` — a small static helper returning true iff `path` equals or is a descendant of `basePath`.
2. NamedScriptResourceCollector: the path-segment branch now normalizes the concatenated path with `ResourceUtil.normalize`, requires `isContained(location.getPath(), path)` to hold, and still applies the existing `SlingServletResolver.isPathAllowed` check (mirroring the sibling "extension" branch that was already safe) before resolving; if any check fails, the method returns early (no children considered) instead of resolving an out-of-tree resource.
3. ResourceCollector: after each selector-driven `resolver.getResource(current, selector)` step, the resulting resource's path is checked with `isContained(location.getPath(), next.getPath())`; if it escaped the subtree, `current` is set to `null`, which naturally ends the do/while descent (matching existing null-handling) instead of continuing to enumerate children of an out-of-tree resource.
4. Regression tests: `NamedScriptResourceCollectorTest` reproduces the original POV scenario (scriptName `"../../../secret/admin/leak"`) inside the standard JUnit test structure and asserts no resource under `/secret` is ever returned, plus a sanity check that the legitimate in-tree script is unaffected. `AbstractResourceCollectorTest.testIsContained` unit-tests the new shared helper directly (exact match, descendant, sibling, ancestor, unrelated path, null).
Both fixes are independent of whether `executionPaths` is configured, closing the gap the alert specifically called out (isPathAllowed being a no-op when unconfigured). The SlingServletResolver.java:457-460 absolute-scriptPath branch was intentionally left unchanged: it already uses the normalize+isPathAllowed pattern (the pattern this fix extends elsewhere) and represents a distinct, intentionally-absolute lookup API rather than a location+fragment concatenation, so adding a "containment" check there is not applicable/would break intended functionality.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk. The change is purely additive validation before two specific resource resolutions; legitimate scriptName/selector values that stay within the resource's own location subtree behave identically to before (verified via the full existing test suite — 167 tests incl. ResourceCollectorTest's 15 ordering/priority tests — all pass unchanged). Behavior change is limited to previously-vulnerable inputs: a scriptName or selector sequence that would have resolved outside the location subtree now yields no candidate for that fragment (NamedScriptResourceCollector returns no results for that location; ResourceCollector simply stops the selector descent early) rather than silently exposing an out-of-tree resource. No API signatures changed; `isContained` is a new protected static helper with no external callers to break. Did not modify the SlingServletResolver absolute-path branch noted in the exploiter's evidence as relying on an unconfigured executionPaths default — that is a distinct, documented feature (arbitrary absolute script path lookup gated by an optional allow-list) rather than a location+fragment concatenation bug, and changing its default-allow semantics risks breaking existing deployments; flagging this for maintainer awareness in case policy hardening (e.g., a secure-by-default executionPaths) is desired separately.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-22 path traversal in the Sling servlet/script resolution machinery. Two call sites built an intermediate resource-lookup path by concatenating a caller/request-controlled fragment (a "named script" name, or a request selector) directly onto a trusted base "location" path, then resolved it via the shared AbstractResourceCollector sink without normalizing or verifying the result stayed inside that location's subtree — unlike a sibling branch in the same method that already does this correctly. Since SlingServletResolver.isPathAllowed() is a permissive no-op whenever the optional executionPaths allow-list is unconfigured (the common default), "../" segments in the script name/selector could escape the intended script folder and reach arbitrary repository resources, which SlingServletResolver would then treat as script/servlet candidates. Added a shared `AbstractResourceCollector.isContained(basePath, path)` containment check and applied it, together with `ResourceUtil.normalize`, at both vulnerable sites: NamedScriptResourceCollector's path-segment branch (the POV's exact target) and ResourceCollector's selector-driven descent. Containment is enforced unconditionally, independent of executionPaths configuration, closing the root cause rather than one path. The absolute-scriptPath branch in SlingServletResolver (already gated by normalize+isPathAllowed, which is the existing "good" pattern the fix mirrors) was left unchanged since it is a distinct, intentionally-absolute lookup API, not a location+fragment concatenation.

parsed_output.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches only: AbstractResourceCollector.java (new `isContained` static helper, well-documented, correct semantics — exact match or `path.startsWith(basePath + '/')`, null-safe), NamedScriptResourceCollector.java (normalizes the concatenated path, requires containment within `location.getPath()`, and still applies the existing `isPathAllowed` check before resolving; returns early with no children if any check fails), ResourceCollector.java (after the selector-driven `resolver.getResource(current, selector)` step, verifies the result stays within `location.getPath()`, nulling `current` otherwise so the existing null-handling in the do/while loop naturally terminates the descent), plus two test files (a new NamedScriptResourceCollectorTest reproducing the PoV scenario and asserting no /secret resource is returned, plus a legit-script sanity check; and a new unit test for the isContained helper directly). No PoV files are modified by the patch (the PoV lives entirely under `.security-pipeline/pov/`, untouched), no functionality is broadly disabled, and the change does not alter the PoV itself. The SlingServletResolver absolute-scriptPath branch (already guarded by normalize+isPathAllowed) was left intentionally unchanged, which is reasonable since it's a distinct, already-safe pattern and not a location+fragment concatenation. This matches the exploiter's stated root cause and the two concrete vulnerable call sites highlighted in the evidence, and is a minimal, targeted vulnerability fix rather than an unrelated behavior change.
parsed_output.pov_result: Independently reran the PoV via the Docker wrapper. On the unpatched baseline (git stash of the 4 tracked patch files, keeping the untracked PoV harness), the PoV passes (exit 0, "OK (1 test)"), confirming the exploit reproduces pre-patch. After restoring the patch (git stash pop), the same PoV fails as expected (exit 1): `AssertionError: Expected NamedScriptResourceCollector to resolve a script OUTSIDE the resource's own resourceType script tree ... found=[]` — the traversal payload no longer resolves any resource, let alone the out-of-tree /secret/admin/leak.esp. This matches the orchestrator's reported pov_before_patch (exit 0) and pov_after_patch (exit 1) results exactly.
parsed_output.regression_result: Independently reran `mvn -B test` via the Docker wrapper against the patched worktree. Result: Tests run: 167, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS — including the new NamedScriptResourceCollectorTest (1/1 pass), the new isContained unit test inside AbstractResourceCollectorTest (7/7 pass), and unmodified ResourceCollectorTest (15/15 pass, covering ordering/priority behavior unaffected by the fix). This matches the orchestrator-reported regression_1 and regression_2 results. (One earlier rerun attempt hit a transient `ClassNotFoundException: org.apache.maven.surefire.junit4.JUnit4Provider` due to a JAR-download race from running the PoV harness and full test suite concurrently against the same shared .m2 cache — a clean immediate rerun succeeded cleanly, so this is environmental flakiness, not a patch regression.)
parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a shared `AbstractResourceCollector.isContained(basePath, path)` containment helper and applies it, together with `ResourceUtil.normalize`, at the two concrete unguarded sinks identified by the exploiter: NamedScriptResourceCollector's script-name path-segment branch (the PoV's exact target) and ResourceCollector's selector-driven descent. Both now mirror the sibling "extension" branch that was already safe, and both enforce containment independent of whether `executionPaths` is configured — closing the gap the alert specifically called out. The fix is minimal, additive, and confined to the vulnerable code paths plus focused regression tests.
